Hi Devon — looping in some technical details ahead of the deep-dive. Short answers below and a suggested test matrix.

Control plane options:
- Managed control plane (Redwood cloud): requires outbound HTTPS to a small set of endpoints for telemetry/management. We can provide a static IP list and FQDNs to allow via egress. No persistent inbound required.
- Customer-managed control plane (Private): we can run the control plane inside your VPC/cluster. In this mode, all control traffic remains inside your network and the Redwood team provides signed packages for updates.

Air-gapped deployment:
- We offer an air-gapped bundle: signed artifacts (runtime + model shards) delivered as tarballs on a secure transfer. Install/upgrade is a manual process run by your infra team.
- For model updates, we support an offline signing workflow and provide checksums and provenance metadata.

Networking specifics (pre-test checklist highlights):
- Egress: https://control.redwood.ai (443), optional metrics endpoint (443). We'll provide a CIDR/IP list.
- Recommended ports for intra-cluster: 7000-7010 (gRPC), 9000 (monitoring) — can be customized.
- Zero-outbound option: available for fully offline mode; requires customer-managed control plane + local artifact import.

Suggested POC test matrix:
1) Networking validation (open the checklist we sent, confirm NACLs/firewall rules).
2) Small-scale on-prem run: single node inference with serialized sample payload (256 tokens) — measure p50/p95.
3) Baseline against Bedrock: run identical payloads and measure latency/cost per 1k tokens.
4) Air-gap install verification: deploy signed artifact and validate model load + inference.

Attachments: redwood-airgap-ops-notes.pdf (detailed steps), plus the checklist Vanessa attached.
